messages:
maria: Prototype for a 'sliding TTL fallback proxy' to smooth region/cost decisioning. TL;DR: short-lived soft fallbacks whose TTL slides on renewals to avoid thundering-herd when region recovers.
alex: high level: how is this different from our existing grace-window / warm pool?
devin: also, does the TTL slide on successful probe or on request touch? :thinking:
maria: slides on successful primary routing / probe. fallback TTL grows on failures, shrinks to base on success. idea is to make fallbacks self-healing but not instant flip-flop.
samir: how does this interact with route cache entries? we already cache route decisions for 10s, so sliding ttl might conflict with cache eviction semantics.
alex: sketch: cache stores {route, expiry, fallback_ttl_meta}. when cache entry expires we keep serving last-known fallback until either a probe replaces it or fallback_ttl expires. avoids immediate thundering restart.
maria: config sketch:```fallback_base_ms = 500
fallback_max_ms = 30000
backoff_multiplier = 2
on_success = fallback_ms = fallback_base_ms
on_fail = fallback_ms = min(fallback_max_ms, fallback_ms * backoff_multiplier)```
devin: we should namespace that per-tenant and per-route class (chat/generation/embedding). different workloads have different tolerance.
samir: question: where does the sliding logic live? policy engine or runtime? owning it in runtime is cheaper but harder to reason about globally.
maria: leaning policy-engine for global consistency: policy returns fallback_window and transition rules; runtime implements local timers and probes. that keeps the decision surface stable and auditable.
alex: agree. policy engine should provide stable parameters and an idempotent extend/mark API like: `POST /policy/v1/fallback/extend {"route_id":"r123","outcome":"success"}` so runtime just informs policy of outcomes.
devin: need metrics: `fallback_count`, `ttl_extensions`, `fallback_duration_ms`, `probe_success_rate` — plus tracing tags for route_id, region, tenant.
ops-bot: infra-note: canary slot available for this on staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC, 2 nodes. ping @maria to schedule.
maria: action items: 1) sim model in routing-sim to validate thundering herd scenarios and cost delta. 2) policy API proto + schema (extend/mark/reset). 3) runtime probe impl and cache shim. 4) add the metrics & dashboard. 5) schedule canary on staging.
alex: small UX ask: add an explainable field in policy response `why_fallback` with reason & last_probe_ts. helps debugging.
samir: also add an opt-out per-tenant flag when they manage their own Dedicated capacity.
devin: I'll pick up sim harness work. maria you own the policy schema. alex will handle explainability field. samir will prototype cache shim.
maria: sounds good. will open RFC follow-up with schema draft and small diagram. thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: please include unit tests for backoff math and a regression test for probe flapping scenarios.
maria: noted, will include tests and a small perf baseline.
